newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hundreds of Hanoi cyclos sent to scrap yard.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of Hanoi cyclos sent to scrap yard.

text.p: Hundreds of bicycle rickshaws, known as cyclos, have been hauled off the streets of Hanoi and sent to the scrap yard in the past 18 months, police in the Vietnamese capital said on Monday.
"We should limit this kind of transport means because they bring traffic chaos, that's the city's policy," a senior officer told Reuters.
He said 305 cyclos which were considered dangerous, unsightly or an obstruction had been confiscated and sent to be used as scrap iron since August 1995.

Cyclos have long been as recognisably Vietnamese as the traditional conical hats or the national dress, the silk ao dai. Many cyclo drivers are war veterans, often wearing green army pith helmets, or migrants from poverty-stricken rural areas.
Now, with growing urban prosperity, they face stiff competition from cut-throat taxi companies and the ubiquitous motorbike.

To make matters worse, municipal authorities in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have made many streets off-limits to cyclos in a bid to restore order to what are perhaps some of the most treacherous roads in Asia.
